newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO SAYS ROMANIA SIGNS SYNDICATED LOAN.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO SAYS ROMANIA SIGNS SYNDICATED LOAN.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO said on Wednesday the terms of a new $175 million syndicated loan arranged by it and Citibank International for the Central Bank of Romania reflected increased confidence in Romania's economy.

"The (loan's) increased life and the lower margin over LIBOR in contrast to previous transactions reflect improved market circumstances for Romanian debt," the bank said in a statement, announcing the signing of the loan.
The facility has a life of three years in contrast to previous loans of one and one-and-a-half years respectively and is priced at 187.5 basis points over LIBOR, a spokesman said.

The previous loan, a $110 million facility issued in December 1995 for 18 months, was priced at 225 b.p. over LIBOR, he said. National Bank of Romania signed the syndicated loan agreement on Wednesday. The syndicate comprises 35 banks.
In May 1995 a $150 million facility marked Romania's return to the capital markets after an absence of over 15 years. The latest loan is the third syndication.
